$description: C1XX Foundations · layout. Breakpoints, gutters, containers, column grid, reading measure and vertical rhythm. All vertical values are multiples of baseline.row (24px) per Müller-Brockmann's grid method.

desktop.$description: > 900 is desktop; ≥ 1280 is where the container caps.

wide.$description: ≥ 1680: display tiers step up to their largest size.

gutter.$description: Page edge padding. Background always reaches the viewport edge; gutters belong to the content.

desktop.$description: Fluid between two scale steps (24 and 72 = 1 and 3 rows).

max.$description: Content never wider than this; project scenes and media may go full-bleed.

columns.$description: Divisible by 2, 3, 4, 6 → thirds, halves, quarters without a second grid.

desktop.$description: = baseline.row, so column gap and row gap share one unit.

row-gap.$description: g × L with g = 1: one empty body row between fields.

measure.$description: Line length in ch of the text tier in use. 7–10 words / 45–75 characters per line.

narrow.$description: Captions, side notes, the lower-right project info block (≈ 330–430px at body size).

wide.$description: Lead paragraphs and statements only; never body copy.

field.$description: Grid field (unit cell) heights = r × L. Image, card and colour-block heights come from these so their edges land on text rows.

span-formula.$description: Height of a block spanning m fields with one empty row between fields.

rhythm.$description: Vertical spacing between blocks, in whole body rows. Component-level spacing lives in spacing.json; this is the layout level.

2.$description: 2 rows — heading to body, card to card.

margin.$description: Page margins are never four-equal: content sits high, bottom margin larger than top.
